newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DUTCH SAY PM KOK WAS REFERRING TO EMU MEMBERS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SAY PM KOK WAS REFERRING TO EMU MEMBERS.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Wednesday that Prime Minister Wim Kok in a statement in Luxembourg had not meant to suggest that the date for choosing participants for a single currency was in doubt.
"He definitely did not mean to say there was uncertainty about the date. The uncertainty to which he referred was to the participants," a Dutch diplomatic source said in Brussels.
The source said the government was preparing a statement in The Hague.

In a speech in Luxembourg earlier, Kok said: "It is uncertain that a decision on the eligibility of the countries participating in Economic and Monetary Union will be taken at the beginning of 1998 under the British presidency of the European Union."

It has been officially agreed that a decision on the participants in the EU's single currency will be made in March or April of 1998 based on data from 1997. The single currency is due to start in 1999. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810
